turns.doctor_question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
turns.patient_response: Well, I, uh... I came in because it's just getting to be too much, you know? It's like... it's like I've got this motor running inside me all day long, just humming and vibrating, and it never shuts off. Never. From the minute I wake up till I finally pass out, it's just go, go, go. And the worst part is when I have to sit still. Oh man, sitting still is just... it's torture. Like, if I'm at church on Sunday, my wife wants me to sit there and listen to the sermon, but after about five minutes, I just feel completely trapped. My skin starts crawling, my legs start bouncing, and I just have to get up. I have to. Same thing happens if I'm waiting here at the clinic, or even just sitting at home trying to watch a TV show with the family. I can't just sit there on the couch. I end up pacing around the living room, or finding some random thing to fix, or just... doing something. Because if I don't move, I feel like I'm gonna explode out of my own skin. It's exhausting, honestly, but I just can't stop it.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient mentions that their legs start bouncing when they try to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient describes having to get up and pace in situations where they are expected to remain seated, such as at church, in the clinic waiting room, or on the couch at home.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes an intense internal feeling of restlessness, stating they feel trapped and like they are going to explode out of their own skin if they don't move.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly states they feel like they have a 'motor running inside' them all day and are constantly 'go, go, go'.

turns.doctor_question: Did this inner restlessness start after you began taking an antidepressant?
turns.patient_response:
An antidepressant? No, no, I don't... I don't take anything like that. I mean, I'm not taking any pills for depression or anything. I don't even really like taking an aspirin unless I absolutely have to, you know? Like if I pull a muscle from pacing around the garage too much or something. But no, this... this feeling, this motor running inside me? It definitely didn't start from a pill. 

It's just... it's always been there. Like, forever. As far back as I can remember, honestly. Even when I was a kid, you know, back before I dropped out of school, I couldn't sit in those little wooden desks. The teachers were always on my case about it, telling me to sit down, stop moving, stop shaking the desk. So it's definitely not from some new medication. 

My wife, she actually asked me a while back if maybe I was depressed, just because I get so worked up and exhausted from all this moving around and not being able to relax with her. But I told her, I said, "I'm not sad, I'm just tired of feeling like I'm gonna crawl out of my own skin!" So, yeah, no antidepressants. Never taken 'em. This is just... it's just how I've always been.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient mentions that teachers used to tell him to stop moving and shaking his desk.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states he couldn't sit in his desk at school and teachers were always telling him to sit down.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes pacing around the garage and feeling like he is going to 'crawl out of my own skin'.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient explicitly describes having a 'motor running inside me'.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies being depressed or sad when his wife asked him about it.

turns.doctor_question: Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
turns.patient_response:
Worrying? No, man, I don't... I don't really do that. I mean, I don't just sit around chewing my fingernails about what-ifs, you know? My wife, now she’s a worrier. She worries enough for the both of us, especially with me not punching a clock right now and all, but me? I don't really get like that. I don't just have these thoughts where I'm scared or fretting over nothing. 

Honestly, I think you gotta be able to actually sit still and think for a minute to worry like that, and like I was saying, I just can't do that. If there's a problem, I just... I jump up and do something about it. Like, last Tuesday, it started raining real hard and my wife was worrying about the gutters backing up because they were full of leaves. She’s standing at the window, all stressed out, wringing her hands. But I didn't sit there and worry with her. I just went right out there in the pouring rain, grabbed the aluminum ladder from the side yard, and started scooping muck out of the gutters with my bare hands. I didn't even put a coat on! I just had to get it done right then, just to be moving, you know? 

And if there ain't a problem to fix, I'm still doing something anyway. I'll be out in the shed taking apart a lawnmower engine that ain't even broken just to see how it looks, or reorganizing the whole garage for the third time this month. So, no, my brain doesn't get stuck on worrying about things. It just gets stuck on going. I don't have the patience to sit and invent things to fret about, I just... I'm just always looking for the next physical thing to do. So, yeah, no. Not a worrier.

symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes being constantly on the go, stating his brain 'gets stuck on going' and he is 'always looking for the next physical thing to do.'
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient describes abnormally increased energy and goal-directed activity, such as reorganizing the garage for the third time in a month and taking apart unbroken engines.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies excessive worrying or fretting over 'what-ifs' or nothing.
